subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: A consignment may be defined as the shipment of goods by a manufacturer or wholesale dealer to-

options.A: an agent for sale on a commission basis
options.B: a customer for sale on a credit basis
options.C: a branch for sale on a cash basis alone
options.D: a purchaser for resale on a profit basis

answer_html:
Answer: (A) an agent for sale on a commission basis.

A consignment may be defined as the shipment of goods by a manufacturer or wholesale dealer to an agent for sale on a commission basis. The agent sells the goods on account of the consignor and the risk is borne by the consignor. It is not a transfer of ownership of goods, but only the sending of goods by one person to another at a different place to be sold by the latter on behalf of the former.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: In a consignment arrangement, the ownership of the goods sent-

options.A: remains with the consignor even after they are sold by the consignee
options.B: remains with the consignor until they are actually sold by the consignee
options.C: passes to the consignee as soon as the goods reach his warehouse
options.D: passes to the consignee as soon as the proforma invoice is received

answer_html:
Answer: (B) remains with the consignor until they are actually sold by the consignee.

The consignor remains the owner of the goods sent on a consignment basis till they are actually sold by the consignee. Only possession, and not ownership, is transferred to the consignee, and the goods consigned to the agent are treated as sales only when they are sold by him.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: When goods are sent by the consignor it is known as an outward consignment, and to the consignee the same is-
answer_html:
Answer: (D) an inward consignment.

When the goods are sent by the consignor it is known as an outward consignment, and to the consignee it is an inward consignment. The consignee does not become the debtor for the goods received on consignment, the relationship between the two parties being that of an agent and a principal only.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: A proforma invoice is-

options.A: a document prepared by the consignor showing the actual cost price of the goods consigned to his agent
options.B: only in the nature of a memorandum invoice and does not make the consignee accountable to pay the amount mentioned in it
options.C: a regular invoice which makes the consignee accountable to pay the amount mentioned in it within the agreed credit period
options.D: a statement prepared by the consignee and sent to the consignor showing the sales made and the expenses incurred

answer_html:
Answer: (B) only in the nature of a memorandum invoice and does not make the consignee accountable to pay the amount mentioned in it.

The proforma invoice is sent by the consignor to the consignee when the goods are sent, and contains information relating to the nature of the goods, the quantity, the weights and the marked price. It is only in the nature of a memorandum invoice and is not a regular invoice, so it does not make the consignee accountable to pay the amount mentioned in it. The price shown is generally not the cost price but sometimes the selling price and sometimes the cost price plus an arbitrary percentage of profit.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: An account sales is a periodical statement prepared by-

options.A: the consignee and sent to the consignor
options.B: the consignor and sent to the consignee
options.C: the consignee and sent to the customers
options.D: the consignor and sent to the customers

answer_html:
Answer: (A) the consignee and sent to the consignor.

An account sales is a periodical statement prepared by the consignee to be sent to the consignor, giving details of all sales whether for cash or on credit, the expenses incurred, the commission due on sales and the goods destroyed in transit or in godown, and deducting the amount of any advance remitted by him. No account sales is required from a buyer to a seller in an ordinary sale.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Del credere commission is the additional commission payable to the consignee for-

options.A: selling the goods at a price above the pre-determined selling price
options.B: bearing out of his own pocket the expenses of receiving and storing the goods
options.C: guaranteeing that the whole of the goods consigned will be sold within the period
options.D: taking over the additional responsibility of collecting money from customers

answer_html:
Answer: (D) taking over the additional responsibility of collecting money from customers.

Del credere commission is an additional commission payable to the consignee for taking over the additional responsibility of collecting money from customers. In case the customers do not pay, the consignee takes over the loss of bad debts in his books. The commission described in Option (A) is the over-riding or special commission, which is paid over and above the ordinary commission.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The loss of goods which occurs due to the inherent nature of the goods involved is-

options.A: an abnormal loss, which is unavoidable and is charged separately to the Profit and Loss Account
options.B: a normal loss, which is unavoidable and forms part of the cost of goods sold
options.C: an abnormal loss, which is avoidable and forms part of the cost of goods sold
options.D: a normal loss, which is avoidable and is charged separately to the Profit and Loss Account

answer_html:
Answer: (B) a normal loss, which is unavoidable and forms part of the cost of goods sold.

A normal loss is the loss of goods which occurs due to the inherent nature of the goods involved. It is by nature an unavoidable loss and forms part of the cost of goods sold, examples being the evaporation of materials and the spillage of liquid materials. An abnormal loss, such as goods pilfered, stolen or lost by fire, is avoidable in nature and is not considered to be a part of the cost of goods sold.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The consignee does not become the debtor for the goods received on consignment because-

options.A: the relationship between the two parties is that of a buyer and a seller
options.B: the goods are always sent to him at a price higher than their cost price
options.C: he is bound to return to the consignor any goods which remain unsold
options.D: the relationship between the two parties is that of an agent and a principal

answer_html:
Answer: (D) the relationship between the two parties is that of an agent and a principal.

The consignee does not become the debtor for the goods received on consignment, the relationship between both the parties being that of an agent and a principal only. He becomes entitled to be reimbursed for the expenses incurred on behalf of the consignor and to receive commission for the goods sold by him only when the goods are actually sold.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Which of the following distinguishes a consignment from a sale?

options.A: The consignee bears the expenses which he incurs, whereas in a sale the seller bears the expenses incurred by the buyer
options.B: The goods are sold against a price in a consignment, whereas in a sale the goods are sold against a commission
options.C: Unsold goods can be returned at any time by the consignee, whereas goods cannot be returned by the buyer after the sale is complete
options.D: The risk of loss passes to the consignee along with possession, whereas in a sale the risk remains with the seller until payment

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Unsold goods can be returned at any time by the consignee, whereas goods cannot be returned by the buyer after the sale is complete.

Among the distinctions drawn, unsold goods can be returned at any time by the consignee if he feels they cannot be sold except at a loss, whereas goods cannot be returned by the buyer after the sale is complete. The risk of loss or damage remains with the consignor till the goods are sold, the consignor usually bears the expenses incurred by the consignee, an account sales is required in a consignment but not in a sale, and goods are sold against commission in a consignment but against a price in a sale.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Over-riding commission is paid when the consignee-

options.A: sells the whole of the consignment within the period fixed by the consignor
options.B: manages to sell the goods above a pre-determined selling price or exceeds the sales target
options.C: guarantees the collection of the money due from the ultimate customers of the goods
options.D: agrees to meet out of his own resources all the expenses of selling the goods

answer_html:
Answer: (B) manages to sell the goods above a pre-determined selling price or exceeds the sales target.

Over-riding commission, also referred to as special commission, is an extra commission which is paid over and above the ordinary commission, and is paid when the consignee manages to sell the goods above a pre-determined selling price or exceeds the sales target. Option (C) describes the del credere commission, which is paid for guaranteeing collection.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Although del credere commission is paid for taking over the risk of bad debts arising out of credit sales only, it is calculated on-

options.A: cash sales and not on credit sales
options.B: the bad debts actually suffered in the period
options.C: total sales and not on credit sales
options.D: credit sales and not on total sales

answer_html:
Answer: (C) total sales and not on credit sales.

Although del credere commission is paid for taking over the risk of bad debts that arise out of credit sales only, this commission is calculated on total sales and not on credit sales. Ordinary commission, by contrast, is payable where the consignee does not guarantee the collection of money from the ultimate customer, and its percentage is generally lower.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The unsold stock lying with the consignee is valued at the cost of the goods sent, adjusted proportionately for-

options.A: the expenses incurred by the consignor and the recurring expenses incurred by the consignee
options.B: the non-recurring expenses incurred by the consignee alone, the consignor's expenses being ignored
options.C: the expenses incurred by the consignor alone, all the consignee's expenses being ignored
options.D: the expenses incurred by the consignor and the non-recurring expenses incurred by the consignee

answer_html:
Answer: (D) the expenses incurred by the consignor and the non-recurring expenses incurred by the consignee.

Where the consignee fails to sell all the goods sent to him, the remaining unsold goods are treated as stock lying with the consignee, and their ownership lies with the consignor. The stock is valued considering the cost of the goods sent, and proportionate adjustments are required for the expenses incurred by the consignor and the non-recurring expenses incurred by the consignee. Recurring expenses such as godown rent and selling expenses are excluded.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: In valuing goods in transit at the close of the accounting period-

options.A: both the consignor's expenses and the consignee's non-recurring expenses are considered
options.B: neither the consignor's nor the consignee's expenses are considered, the cost alone being taken
options.C: the expenses incurred by the consignor are considered but no expenses incurred by the consignee are included
options.D: the expenses incurred by the consignee are considered but no expenses incurred by the consignor are included

answer_html:
Answer: (C) the expenses incurred by the consignor are considered but no expenses incurred by the consignee are included.

Goods in transit are goods despatched by the consignor which have yet to reach the consignee, and their ownership lies with the consignor. They are valued after considering the expenses incurred by the consignor, and no expenses incurred by the consignee are to be included in valuing the same, since the consignee has not yet received the goods and can have incurred nothing on them.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where the net realisable value of the unsold consignment stock falls below its cost, the stock is valued at-

options.A: the average of the cost and the net realisable value on the date of the balance sheet
options.B: the invoice price at which the goods were originally sent by the consignor to his agent
options.C: net realisable value, being the expected selling price less the incidental expenses of making the sale
options.D: cost, the fall in the market being recognised only in the year in which the stock is actually sold

answer_html:
Answer: (C) net realisable value, being the expected selling price less the incidental expenses of making the sale.

As per AS-2, unsold stock is to be valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower. Net realisable value means the expected selling price less the incidental expenses of making such a sale, and when it falls below cost the consignment stock is to be valued at the lower net realisable value.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where goods are sent at invoice price, the entry for the cancellation of the load on the closing stock is-

options.A: Consignment A/c Dr., to Consignment Stock Reserve A/c
options.B: Consignment Stock Reserve A/c Dr., to Consignment A/c
options.C: Stock on Consignment A/c Dr., to Consignment A/c
options.D: Goods Sent on Consignment A/c Dr., to Consignment A/c

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Consignment A/c Dr., to Consignment Stock Reserve A/c.

Where goods are sent at invoice price the Consignment Account stands debited with the invoice price, so adjustments are needed to ascertain the correct profit. The load on the closing stock is cancelled by debiting the Consignment A/c and crediting the Consignment Stock Reserve A/c. The entry in Option (B) cancels the load on the opening stock, and that in Option (D) cancels the load on the goods sent less returns.
topic_text: Cancellation of load on closing stock

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where the consignee is not paid any del credere commission, a bad debt arising on a credit sale is recorded in the books of the consignor by-

options.A: debiting the Consignee's Personal A/c and crediting the Consignment A/c
options.B: passing no entry at all, the loss being borne by the consignee himself
options.C: debiting the Consignment A/c and crediting the Consignment Debtors A/c
options.D: debiting the Consignment Debtors A/c and crediting the Consignment A/c

answer_html:
Answer: (C) debiting the Consignment A/c and crediting the Consignment Debtors A/c.

Where no del credere commission is given, the credit sale is recorded by the consignor by debiting the Consignment Debtors A/c, and the bad debt is borne by the consignor by debiting the Consignment A/c and crediting the Consignment Debtors A/c. It is only where del credere commission is given that the consignor passes no entry for the bad debt, the consignee then recording it in his own books.
topic_text: Bad debts without del credere commission

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Ram & Co. consigned 50 cases costing ₹200 each to Nathan, paying insurance ₹200 and freight ₹300. Nathan sold the whole consignment for ₹24,000, incurred dock dues ₹20, carriage ₹50 and warehousing expenses ₹130, and is entitled to commission at 4% on sales. The profit on consignment and the amount remitted by Nathan are respectively-
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹12,340 and ₹22,840.

The Consignment Account is debited with the cost of ₹10,000, the consignor's expenses of ₹500, the consignee's expenses of ₹200 and commission of 4% on ₹24,000, that is ₹960, and credited with sales of ₹24,000, leaving a profit of ₹12,340. Nathan remits ₹24,000 less his expenses of ₹200 and his commission of ₹960, that is ₹22,840.

question_html: K sent 1,000 boxes of clothing to P on consignment. P sold 500 boxes at ₹250 per box and 300 boxes at ₹260 per box, and is entitled to commission at 7% on gross sales. The commission payable is-

Answer: (A) ₹14,210.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: A consignee sold 5,000 sarees at ₹125 per saree and is entitled to commission of 5% on total sales plus a further 25% commission on any surplus price realised over ₹120 per saree. The total commission is-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) ₹37,500.

Total sales are 5,000 sarees at ₹125, that is ₹6,25,000, and the amount at ₹120 per saree is ₹6,00,000, so the surplus price realised is ₹25,000. Commission at 5% on total sales is ₹31,250, to which is added 25% on the surplus of ₹25,000, that is ₹6,250, making ₹37,500 in all.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
case_facts_html:
A consigned to B 5,000 kg of tea costing ₹40 per kg. A incurred ₹3,000 on freight and ₹2,000 on insurance.

500 kg of tea were lost in transit, and the insurance company admitted a claim for ₹15,000. After receiving the goods B spent ₹1,000 on carriage, ₹500 on selling and ₹500 on godown rent, and is allowed commission at 5% on sales.

3,000 kg of tea were sold at ₹64 per kg. A further 25 kg of tea were lost owing to the breakage of a chest, which was considered to be normal.
question_html: Refer to the first case scenario. The value of the abnormal loss of 500 kg lost in transit is-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹20,500.

The cost of 5,000 kg at ₹40 per kg is ₹2,00,000, to which are added the expenses incurred by the consignor before the loss occurred, namely freight ₹3,000 and insurance ₹2,000, giving ₹2,05,000 for 5,000 kg. The value of 500 kg is therefore ₹2,05,000 multiplied by 500 and divided by 5,000, that is ₹20,500. The ₹15,000 in Option (B) is merely the claim admitted by the insurer.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
case_facts_html:
T of Jamshedpur consigned goods costing ₹2,00,000 to his agent P of Patna. The invoice was made pro forma so as to show a profit of 25% on cost.

T paid ₹4,000 for freight and insurance. P sold part of the consignment for ₹1,76,000 at a uniform price of 10% over the invoice price, and spent ₹6,000 as warehousing charges and ₹2,000 as selling expenses.

P is entitled to a commission of 5% on sales and a further 20% of the net profit after charging the commission on sales.
question_html: Refer to the second case scenario. The invoice price of the goods sent and the loading contained in it are respectively-
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹2,50,000 and ₹50,000.

The invoice price is the cost price plus a profit of 25% on cost, that is ₹2,00,000 plus ₹50,000, giving ₹2,50,000, and the loading is accordingly ₹50,000. Had the profit been 25% on the invoice price instead, the loading would have worked out differently, which is the trap in Option (D).

question_html: Refer to the second case scenario. The stock reserve to be created against the closing stock is-
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹18,000.

The invoice price of the goods sold is ₹1,76,000 divided by 110 and multiplied by 100, that is ₹1,60,000, so the invoice price of the stock on consignment is ₹2,50,000 less ₹1,60,000, that is ₹90,000. The loading on that stock is ₹90,000 multiplied by 25 and divided by 125, that is ₹18,000, and this is the stock reserve. The reserve is computed on the invoice price alone and not on the proportionate expenses added to it.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: K sent 1,000 boxes costing ₹200 each to P and paid railway freight and insurance of ₹500. P incurred carriage of ₹100 and other charges of ₹2,000, and 200 boxes remained unsold. The value of the unsold stock is-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹40,120.

The value of the 200 boxes unsold is ₹2,00,600 multiplied by 200 and divided by 1,000, that is ₹40,120. The other charges of ₹2,000 are recurring in nature and are excluded, their inclusion giving the figure in Option (D).

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: M was allowed commission of 6% on sales of ₹23,000, including 1% for the del credere arrangement. A debtor for ₹2,000 became insolvent and only 50 paise in the rupee was recovered. In M's books, the amount transferred from the Commission Received Account to the Profit and Loss Account is-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) ₹380.

The commission received is 6% of ₹23,000, that is ₹1,380, made up of ordinary commission of 5%, namely ₹1,150, and del credere commission of 1%, namely ₹230. As del credere commission has been allowed, the consignee bears the bad debt of ₹1,000, being one half of ₹2,000, and it is written off against the Commission Received Account, leaving ₹380 to be transferred to the Profit and Loss Account.
topic_text: Bad debt absorbed out of commission

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: K sent goods costing ₹1,00,000 to D, paying railway freight ₹5,000 and insurance ₹2,000. D sold the entire quantity for ₹1,50,000, of which ₹30,000 was on credit, and a customer owing ₹5,000 failed to pay. D was allowed commission of 10% on sales but no del credere commission. The profit on consignment is-
answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹23,000.

The Consignment Account is debited with goods sent ₹1,00,000, freight ₹5,000, insurance ₹2,000, commission of 10% on ₹1,50,000, that is ₹15,000, and the bad debt of ₹5,000, which the consignor bears because no del credere commission was allowed, making ₹1,27,000 in all. Against sales of ₹1,50,000 the profit is therefore ₹23,000; ignoring the bad debt would give the ₹28,000 in Option (A).
